paper_style.palette_strategy: Tables use black/white rules and mathematical text, with pink theorem links and blue reference links. Experimental plots use a Matplotlib-like blue main series, red dashed comparison/reference, orange and green ε series, pale blue repeat bands, and gray grids. Proof diagrams use pale blue/green fills, pink hatching, or pale lavender emphasis; colors are locally semantic rather than one global method palette.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: All 50 pages were inspected from 200 dpi renders. pdfimages -list reports no embedded raster objects; table rules, captions, diagrams, plotted curves, labels, and fonts render as PDF vector/text objects. The PNGs are audit renders only, not paper assets.
paper_style.style_consistency: Computer Modern Roman/Math is stable across body text, captions, tables, formulas, and proof diagrams; DejaVu Sans/Oblique is consistently used for the small experimental plot labels. Table line conventions are stable, but late empirical plots use very small type and varying local color roles.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Exponent of n (left plot) and exponent of ε (right plot) for the problem of computing s(K) up to a 1 + ε factor. For the left plot, note that there is never a reason to spend more than ω(n) time since a simple Chernoff bound calculation shows that sampling Õ(n/ε²) uniformly random entries also suffices to 1 + ε approximate s(K). Thus, we may always take the minimum of the exponent of [BIMW21] and 1. Note that the interesting regime of p is 0 ≤ p ≤ 1, with the best p values given in Table 3.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1: Summary of our upper bound results for the Gaussian kernel matrix. p_g = 0.173 + o(1) [CKNS20] denotes the best known exponent for the Gaussian kernel [CKNS20] The prior results are from [BIMW21], which are the fastest theoretical algorithms, to the best of our knowledge. The “Improvement Factor” column highlights the asymptotic reduction in complexity provided by our algorithms. All upper bounds are also multiplied by d (including those of [BIMW21]) which we omit for simplicity. We also omit all +o(1) factors in the exponents for simplicity. We refer to the specific theorems for details.

tables.uncertainty: Theoretical asymptotic upper bounds only; tilde-O hides polylogarithmic factors, exponents omit +o(1), and d is omitted for simplicity. No statistical interval, repetition, or empirical uncertainty is reported.
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows are non-negative matrix-vector product, top eigenvalue, non-negative vector-matrix-vector product, and kernel sum. Columns encode the authors’ Gaussian upper bound, BIMW21 prior work, and the asymptotic improvement factor; entries are symbolic n/ε exponents with p_g=0.173+o(1), not point estimates from sampled data.
tables.evidence_relation: §2 Gaussian results summary → Table 1 task/prior/improvement index → Theorems 2.1–2.4 and detailed §6–§9 proofs. Table 2 handles lower bounds separately and Figures 4–10 test only selected practical behavior.
design_strengths: The task, prior cost, and improvement factor share one decision surface.
The long caption explicitly defines p_g and the omitted factors, while theorem links keep each row auditable.
design_weaknesses: Long task labels and formulas make the four-row table vertically dense.
Improvement is expressed only through asymptotic exponents; input restrictions and practical implementation cost remain outside the table.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use task–ours–prior–improvement columns for theorem summaries, with a table note that centralizes hidden dimensions and lower-order factors.

evidence.label: p.3 Table 1 Gaussian upper-bound summary and caption

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2: Summary of our lower bounds. 1st row: [BIMW21] gave a lower bound of Ω(√n). See the theorems for details.

tables.uncertainty: Conditional complexity lower bounds rather than statistical uncertainty: the four nearly-quadratic rows rely on SETH/OV reductions, while the sampling row records the BIMW21 lower bound.
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows cover required row/column samples for s(K), non-negative vᵀKw, asymmetric kernel sum, asymmetric top singular value, and asymmetric non-negative MVP. The right column uses Ω(√n/ε²) or Ω(n^{2−α}) for any α>0; theorem links and SETH text carry the conditions.
tables.evidence_relation: §2.4 lower-bound summary → Table 2 → Theorems 2.5/2.7 and Corollaries 11.1–11.3. Figure 3 supplies the vᵀKw reduction layout; Figure 2 belongs to the separate kernel-sum algorithm/limit narrative.
design_strengths: Short task labels and a common asymptotic notation make the hardness boundary scannable.
The caption reconnects the first row to BIMW21 while the theorem links identify the formal source for every other row.
design_weaknesses: SETH is not a separate column or header flag, so conditionality is easy to miss in an isolated table view.
The “1st row” note is terse and does not define every abbreviation or distinguish asymmetric from symmetric cases in the header.
tables.reusable_pattern: When mixing sample and conditional hardness rows, keep each task’s assumption in the row text and point to the full theorem in the caption.

evidence.label: p.4 Table 2 lower-bound summary and caption

caption.text: Table 3: Results for kernel density estimation queries that can be used in Definition 6.1. Note that p < 1 in all cases. The stated result in the last row assumes β ≥ 0 and β = O(1). cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Main p.1–12 uses Table 1 for Gaussian upper bounds and Table 2 for lower-bound boundaries. Appendix-style p.13–15 adds Table 3 and Figure 1 for kernel exponents, Figures 2–3 visualize proof interfaces, and §12 Figures 4–10 proceed from the core ε/error relation to noise-floor trajectories, bandwidth robustness, Nystrom baseline, wall-clock crossover, scale sweep, and primitive query-count comparison.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Every caption starts with Figure/Table n. Table 1/3 and Figure 1/5 provide long setup/condition text; Figures 4–9 explain the main variables and selected findings, while Figure 10 is only a title-like comparison sentence. The at-least-20-repetition/one-SD convention is stated once on p.40 rather than in each empirical caption.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: All three tables use one-level headers: Table 1 is task/ours/prior/improvement, Table 2 is task/lower bound, and Table 3 is kernel/function/p/reference. Mathematical notation is embedded directly in headers and cells; theorem/reference hyperlinks use text color but there is no table legend.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Table 1/2 summarize theorem-level claims; Table 3 supplies the Fast KDE interface parameter. Figures 1–3 explain kernel-sum and OV mechanisms. Figure 4 is the direct Algorithm 2/Theorem 6.3 empirical bridge; Figure 5 is its failure/noise-floor diagnostic; Figures 6/9 are scale robustness, Figure 7 is Nystrom comparison, and Figures 8/10 are wall-clock and query-count efficiency views. No separate training ablation is present.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: The author explicitly separates main-body Gaussian focus from appendix coverage of other kernels and full proofs. Main p.1–12 has two tables and no figures; appendix-style p.13–47 contains Table 3 and all ten figures, with §12 empirical results late and Figures 8–10 floated after the p.45 References heading. The main tables point to the theorem/proof material rather than duplicating it.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Computer Modern Roman/Math ties captions, tables, equations, and proof diagrams together; DejaVu Sans keeps plot labels consistent across Figures 1 and 4–10. Estimated plot text is only about 5–7 pt, so typographic family consistency does not remove small-size readability problems.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Blue is usually the authors’/approximate series, red often denotes prior or exact reference, pale blue denotes spread, and gray denotes grid/repeated runs; orange/green encode ε levels in Figure 9. The diagrams and tables use different local fills/text-link colors, and multicolor curve roles are not uniformly grayscale-safe.

most_reusable_patterns: Table 1’s task–ours–prior–improvement structure binds asymptotic claims to theorem rows.
Figure 4’s common estimand and dataset facets turn a scaling prediction into a direct cross-dataset visual test.
Figure 5 preserves repeated trajectories, while Figure 8 pairs size facets with an exact-runtime baseline and Figure 10 isolates primitive query count.
highest_value_objects: Table 1: the most compact auditable summary of the upper-bound contribution and prior-work reduction.
Figure 4: the clearest empirical bridge for the δ=Θ(ε) top-eigenvalue claim.
Figure 5: the strongest diagnostic of convergence and the MVP-noise error floor.
Figure 8: the most operational comparison of approximate versus exact computation on the stated hardware.
failure_patterns: All ten figures are in appendix-style late pages; Figures 8–10 are even separated from §12 by the References float.
Repetition and one-standard-deviation semantics are global prose rather than object-level captions, and several captions omit aggregation or denominator details.
Small multi-panel plots rely on color and repeated legends; Figure 4/6/9 are not robustly grayscale-safe, and panel-specific ranges complicate cross-panel comparison.
No publicly verified author plotting/table/LaTeX source was found, so visual properties cannot be promoted to source_exact.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper fixes theorem-level upper and lower bounds in two main tables, then uses appendix-style proof diagrams and progressively narrower empirical facets to constrain ε precision, noise floors, baseline sample cost, and practical runtime/query trade-offs.
